title: Shraddha Kapoor Is Playing Maharashtra's Most Legendary Dancer. Nobody Saw This Coming.
excerpt: After Stree 2's ₹857-crore rampage, Bollywood's biggest female star disappears into a Tamasha biopic directed by the man behind Chhaava — and lands it on Rakshabandhan.
body:
There is a version of **Shraddha Kapoor's** career that writes itself. You do *Stree 3*. You do another horror-comedy. You ride the franchise wave until it breaks. That version is easy, predictable, and worth several hundred crores.

Shraddha chose the other version.

**Eetha**, her next film, has locked its theatrical release for **August 28, 2026** — right in the Rakshabandhan window, one of the most coveted slots on the Bollywood calendar. And instead of returning to the supernatural universe that made her the most bankable actress in Indian cinema, she's playing **Vithabai Narayangaonkar**, the legendary Tamasha and Lavani artist who is to Maharashtra's folk performance tradition what Lata Mangeshkar was to playback singing: foundational, irreplaceable, and largely unknown outside the state.

This is not a safe choice. It's a thrilling one.

## The Woman Behind the Legend

Vithabai Narayangaonkar was a force of nature. Born into a tradition that was simultaneously celebrated and stigmatized, she turned the Tamasha stage — a form of Maharashtrian folk theatre built on dance, music, satire, and raw sensuality — into something that commanded respect from the very establishment that had looked down on it. Lavani, the dance form she mastered, is physically demanding, emotionally exposed, and culturally loaded in ways that make even seasoned performers hesitate.

Shraddha reportedly spent months in preparation, working with Lavani practitioners and immersing herself in the rhythms of a performance tradition that requires not just choreography but an entirely different relationship with your body, your audience, and the stage. The shoot wrapped recently after an extended schedule across Maharashtra, with the production reportedly mounted on a scale that reflects how seriously **Maddock Films** and director **Laxman Utekar** are treating the material.

> "It is one of the most challenging roles of her career."
> — Industry source, Sacnilk

## Utekar's Hot Streak

Utekar is not messing around. His last film, **Chhaava**, was a blockbuster. Before that: *Mimi*, which gave Kriti Sanon a National Award, and *Luka Chuppi*, which announced him as a director who could balance commercial instincts with genuine storytelling ambition. He's built a reputation for turning female-led stories into box office events without diluting their substance.

With *Eetha*, he's doing something even more specific — crafting what's being described as a heartfelt tribute to Maharashtra's folk culture, complete with elaborate song sequences and period detailing. For diaspora audiences who grew up hearing about Tamasha but never quite saw it given the cinematic treatment it deserves, this could be revelatory.

## The Box Office Equation

Let's talk numbers, because Shraddha's position in the industry right now is genuinely unprecedented for a female star. **Stree 2** grossed ₹857 crore worldwide with a 946% return on investment — the highest ROI of any Bollywood film in 2024. She didn't just open a film; she carried it past every male-led release that year.

That kind of commercial gravity means *Eetha* arrives with enormous expectations. The Rakshabandhan release window adds another layer — it's a family-friendly holiday slot, and a biographical drama about a folk artist fits the mood better than another franchise sequel might.

The film will reportedly clash with **Sidharth Malhotra's** *Vvan*, but if Shraddha's *Stree 2* numbers are any indication, that's less a clash and more a scheduling inconvenience for the other film.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

Tamasha and Lavani are art forms that most NRIs have only encountered in fragments — a wedding performance here, a YouTube clip there. A major Bollywood production anchored by a star of Shraddha's magnitude could do for these traditions what *Lagaan* did for cricket dramas or *Gangubai Kathiawadi* did for the conversation around Mumbai's underbelly. It makes the invisible visible.

The film is a **Maddock Films** production — the same banner behind the entire Maddock Supernatural Universe, *Chhaava*, and a string of commercial hits. Producer **Dinesh Vijan** has been on an extraordinary run, and pairing him with Utekar and Shraddha on a story this culturally rich feels like the kind of bet that either wins everything or announces a new creative direction for all three.

*Eetha* arrives in theatres on **August 28, 2026**. Mark the date. Shraddha Kapoor isn't playing it safe — and that's exactly why this might be the most important Hindi film of the year.
